papers.title: The Effect of Mini-Batch Noise on the Implicit Bias of Adam
papers.findings: Definition3.1 uses bias-corrected mini-batch Adam with epsilon inside the square root. TheoremB.1 assumes C3 per-sample losses with uniformly bounded first three derivatives on an open convex domain and gives O(eta^2) trajectory approximation for O(eta^-1) steps. Theorem3.3 is a second-order noise expansion; Section3.3 additionally averages coordinate noise ratios and discards/interprets other terms to obtain directional sharpness predictions.
papers.limits: Specified main sections and TheoremB.1 statement read; full proofs, experiments and upstream code not audited. No clipping/AdamW theorem for the exact native pipeline was established. Neither small eta alone nor the paper title provides an empirical error bound for fresh5. Sharpness is a proxy, not a theorem of held-out Macro gain.

papers.title: High-probability convergence of adaptive, proximal, and clipped Adam-type methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization
papers.findings: Eq2/p4 uses a predictable preconditioner from past gradients. Assumptions1-5 include smoothness, deterministic metric bounds, conditionally unbiased sub-Gaussian noise and bounded true gradients. Section6/Theorem6.1 clips gradient noise relative to the true gradient. Section7/Theorem7.1 adds explicit predictive momentum alignment; the conclusion controls stationarity rather than classification utility.
papers.limits: Selected setup and Sections6/7 statements/derivations read, not complete proofs or numerical experiments. The noise-clipping operator and lagged preconditioner differ from the native total-gradient clipping and current-gradient second moment. Momentum alignment and unbiasedness are not verified for native random-reshuffling training. JOTA template is not proof of publication.

papers.title: Quantum Lazy Training
papers.findings: Eq11-13 uses an m^-1/2 sum of geometrically local observables. Theorem1 assumes geometric locality and independent random circuit parameters. Theorem2 analyzes gradient flow for squared-error learning; changes of parameters/kernel and linearization error shrink with growing qubit count under stated initial-loss/time conditions.
papers.limits: Selected abstract, setup and theorem sections read; not whole proofs, experiments or code. Native three-qubit learned prepare/effect Born scores, token normalization, signed affine head, CE and finite AdamW do not instantiate a demonstrated growing-m local-observable family. Non-application establishes neither lazy behavior nor feature learning in fresh5.
